q1: SELECT b.name AS bar, COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker) AS num_drinker, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price, (SELECT f1.drinker FROM frequents AS f1 WHERE f1.bar = b.name ORDER BY f1.times_a_week DESC, f1.drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM bar AS b LEFT JOIN frequents AS f ON b.name = f.bar LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.bar GROUP BY b.name ORDER BY num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC
q2: WITH DrinkerFrequentsBar AS (SELECT drinker, bar, times_a_week AS taw FROM frequents), BarServesBeerPrice AS (SELECT bar, beer, price FROM serves), TotalDrinkersWhoFrequentBar AS (SELECT bar, COUNT(DISTINCT drinker) AS tnd FROM DrinkerFrequentsBar AS f GROUP BY bar), BarAveragePriceOfBeerServed AS (SELECT bar, AVG(price) AS ap FROM BarServesBeerPrice AS s GROUP BY bar), BarMaxTAW AS (SELECT bar, MAX(taw) AS max_taw FROM DrinkerFrequentsBar AS f GROUP BY bar), BarAndMultipleMRDrinkers AS (SELECT mtaw.bar AS bar, f.drinker AS drinker FROM BarMaxTAW AS mtaw INNER JOIN DrinkerFrequentsBar AS f ON mtaw.bar = f.bar AND mtaw.max_taw = f.taw), BarAndOneMRDrinker AS (SELECT mtaw.bar, MIN(mtaw.drinker) AS drinker FROM BarAndMultipleMRDrinkers AS mtaw GROUP BY mtaw.bar) SELECT t.bar AS bar, t.tnd AS total_num_drinker, a.ap AS avg_price, m.drinker AS most_reg_drinker FROM TotalDrinkersWhoFrequentBar AS t, BarAveragePriceOfBeerServed AS a, BarAndOneMRDrinker AS m WHERE t.bar = a.bar AND t.bar = m.bar ORDER BY t.tnd DESC, m.drinker ASC

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses a subquery to find the most regular drinker for each bar, while Q2 uses a CTE to achieve the same result. The difference arises when there are multiple drinkers with the same highest frequency of visits to a bar. In Q1, the subquery uses ORDER BY f1.times_a_week DESC, f1.drinker ASC, which means that if there are multiple drinkers with the same highest frequency, the one with the lexicographically smallest name is chosen. In Q2, the CTE uses ORDER BY f.taw DESC, f.drinker ASC, which achieves the same result. However, the difference becomes apparent when the data is inconsistent or when the data is updated. In such cases, the results of Q1 and Q2 may differ.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have multiple drinkers with the same highest frequency of visits to a bar, and the lexicographically smallest name should be different from the one used in the subquery of Q1.
